title: RFP Brief
description: Structured extraction of an RFP and accompanying client inputs. Stage 2 output.

legal_name.description: Exact legal entity name as written in the RFP

term.description: Contract duration as stated, e.g. '18 months + 12 month option'

requirements.description: Every distinct ask. IDs are the spine of the run — Stage 3 maps to them, Stage 6 checks coverage against them.

text.description: The client's own wording, not a paraphrase

kind.description: What answering it actually means, which is not the same for every requirement. proposal-content: the response must describe something ('the Tenderer shall provide a Transition Management plan') — a slide covers it. delivery-obligation: something we must do after award ('the Contractor shall collect evaluation forms within seven days') — the deck commits to it, usually inside the relevant approach section. commercial-constraint: a pricing or cost condition ('at no additional cost to the Authority') — belongs in commercials. submission-rule: governs the response document itself (format, page limit, naming) — no slide covers it; Stage 6 checks the deck against it instead.

note.description: Required when confidence is 'inferred' — what is ambiguous and why

cm_scope.description: Which parts of the RFP the CM response actually answers. Stage 2 writes this from triage_rfp.py plus its own read. It exists so the decision to leave a clause out is recorded rather than implied — on a full multi-part tender most of the document is not CM's to answer, and the risk is dropping the one buried clause that is.

triage_ref.description: Path to rfp_triage.json, when the triage script was run

in_scope_sections.description: Clauses or chapters the CM response answers, in the RFP's own numbering

ref.description: Clause or section reference, e.g. '3.1.2(g)' or 'Part 2, Ch 8'

why.description: What makes it CM's to answer

reviewed_and_excluded.description: Sections read and judged not CM's to answer. Recording them is the point: a section absent from both lists was never read.

why.description: e.g. 'hardware warranty terms — no change or training content'

not_supplied.description: Parts the RFP cross-references that we were not given. Each is a hole in the read, not an absence of requirements.

weight.description: Percentage. null when the RFP does not state one — do not guess

submission_deadline.description: ISO 8601 with timezone — RFP deadlines are precise

prescribed_structure.description: Response structure the RFP mandates. When present, Stage 3 mirrors this order.

named_deliverables.description: Deliverables the RFP names in its own words. Drives section naming (mirror the client's term) and, when no evaluation weights are published, section sizing. A named deliverable must have a home in the response.

canonical_section.description: Which section of the library this maps to, e.g. 'change-impact-assessment'. Omit when the RFP names something the canonical list does not carry — those still need a home.

emphasis_clauses.description: How many clauses the RFP spends on it. The sizing signal when weights are absent.

optional_scope.description: Priced as an option for the client to exercise

context.description: Feeds the 'Our Understanding of Your Situation' section

delivery_methodology.description: Shapes the whole CM approach — when change activity happens and what it attaches to. Read from the RFP's vocabulary; if not-stated, ask rather than assume and record it in open_questions.

methodology_evidence.description: The terms and clauses the methodology call was read from, so it is auditable

open_questions.description: Material ambiguities worth a clarification question before the clarification deadline

sources.description: Every input document parsed in Stage 1
